items.title: Section: What Is Enjoyed, What Is Finally Realised, and Three Kinds of Seeking

items.zh: 又婆羅門所受用法，受用障道塗飾、香鬘、莊嚴具等，又現受用歌舞、作倡、戲笑等事，又現受用婬欲等法，故是下劣。沙門所有受用之法，受用無罪正聞思修所成智慧，故是勝妙。又婆羅門所有證法，但以梵世為究竟故，復退還故，雜染污故，有苦惱故，是其下劣。沙門證法，以般涅槃為究竟故，無退轉故，一向離垢故，一向安樂故，當知勝妙。復次，欲求有五。一、攝受求，二、受用求，三、戲樂求，四、乏解了求，五、名聲求。有求亦五。一、法爾求，二、祈願求，三、愚癡求，四、厭患求，五、思擇求。
items.en: The brahmins enjoy ornamentation, song, dance, and sexual pleasure, obstacles to the path, and so are inferior; the renunciants enjoy only faultless wisdom born of hearing, reflection, and cultivation, and so are superior. The brahmins' own realisation culminates only in the Brahma world, still subject to falling back, mixed with defilement, and touched by suffering, and so is inferior; the renunciants' realisation culminates in nirvana, never falling back, entirely free of stain, and entirely at peace, and so is superior. Seeking after desire has five aspects. Seeking after existence also has five: seeking naturally, seeking through vow, seeking through delusion, seeking through aversion, and seeking through discernment.

items.title: Section: Genuine Seeking After Liberation, Closing the Renunciant's Own Portrait

items.zh: 梵行求亦五。一、唯求求，二、趣向求，三、現得求，四、後得求，五、思擇當得求。復有差別。謂假名求、第一義求、彼觀察求、無方便求、有方便求。
items.en: Seeking after pure conduct also has five aspects: seeking alone, seeking that heads towards attainment, seeking present attainment, seeking future attainment, and discerning seeking of future attainment. There is a further distinction: nominal seeking, ultimate seeking, observational seeking, seeking without skilful means, and seeking with skilful means.

items.title: Section: Why Inner Knowledge Outshines Every Other Science

items.zh: 如本地分中已說五明處。其內明處，於諸明處諸論、諸宗，為最為勝。何以故？由四清淨清淨義故。一、攝一切染淨義清淨故；二、即此義非他論所制伏清淨故；三、即此義易可入清淨故；四、既得入已，正行不壞清淨故。
items.en: As already explained in the Grounds of Wisdom Attained through Hearing, there are five sciences. Inner knowledge is supreme among every doctrine and school found in all these sciences. Why is this so? Because of four kinds of purity: encompassing every meaning of defilement and purity; being unrefuted by other doctrines; being easy to enter; and, once entered, its practice remaining unspoiled.

items.title: Section: Ten Topics That Comprise the Buddha's Entire Teaching

items.zh: 復次，諸佛聖教若欲略釋，由六種理門應隨決了。一、真義理門，二、證得理門，三、教導理門，四、遠離二邊理門，五、不可思議理門，六、意趣理門。此中前三理門，由後三理門應隨決了。謂真義理門，由遠離二邊理門應隨決了；證得理門，由不可思議理門應隨決了；教導理門，由意趣理門應隨決了。
items.en: Furthermore, if the Buddhas' noble teaching is to be briefly explained, it should be discerned through six gateways of reasoning: the gateway of true meaning, the gateway of realisation, the gateway of teaching, the gateway of avoiding two extremes, the gateway of the inconceivable, and the gateway of intention. Among these, the first three gateways are discerned through the latter three: the gateway of true meaning is discerned through the gateway of avoiding two extremes; the gateway of realisation is discerned through the gateway of the inconceivable; and the gateway of teaching is discerned through the gateway of intention.

items.zh: 此中真義即是理門，是故名為真義理門；乃至意趣即是理門，是故名為意趣理門。理門義者，謂於彼彼無顛倒性、如其實性、離顛倒性。

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Truth, from What Everyone Agrees On to What Cannot Be Said at All

items.zh: 復次，應知真義略有六種。謂世間所成真實，乃至所知障淨智所行真實、安立真實、非安立真實。前四真實，應知如前菩薩地中已廣分別。云何安立真實？謂四聖諦。苦由苦故，乃至道由道故。所以者何？以略安立三種世俗。一、世間世俗，二、道理世俗，三、證得世俗。
items.en: One should know that true meaning is, briefly, of six kinds: truth established by worldly agreement, through the object of wisdom purified of the cognitive obstruction, established truth, and non-established truth. What is established truth? The four noble truths, suffering as suffering, and so on through the path as path. There are, briefly, three kinds of worldly convention: convention of the world, convention of reasoning, and convention of realisation.

items.zh: 世間世俗者，所謂安立宅舍、瓶瓫、軍林、數等，又復安立我、有情等。道理世俗者，所謂安立蘊、界、處等。證得世俗者，所謂安立預流果等彼所依處。

items.title: Section: A Fourth Convention for the Truth Beyond All Words

items.zh: 又復安立略有四種。謂如前說三種世俗，及與安立勝義世俗。即勝義諦。由此諦義不可安立，內所證故，但為隨順發生此智，是故假立。云何非安立真實？謂諸法真如。云何證得？
items.en: There are also, briefly, four kinds of convention: the three kinds of worldly convention already stated, together with the convention of ultimate truth, namely the ultimate truth itself. Because the meaning of this truth cannot be conventionally established, being realised directly within, it is only provisionally established in order to give rise to this wisdom accordingly. What is non-established truth? The suchness of all phenomena. What is realisation?

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Realisation, from Ordinary Karma to the Śrāvaka's Own Five

items.zh: 謂若略說有四證得。一、諸有情業果證得，二、聲聞乘證得，三、獨覺乘證得，四、大乘證得。有情業果證得者，謂由所作淨不淨業自所作業為依因故，諸有情類，於五趣等生死海中感異熟果、受異熟果。聲聞乘證得者，謂先受歸依，乃至沙門莊嚴為依因故，有五種證得。一、地證得，二、智證得，三、淨證得，四、果證得，五、功德證得。
items.en: Realisation is, briefly, of four kinds: the realisation of beings' own karmic fruit, that is, their actually receiving it, realisation belonging to the śrāvaka vehicle, realisation belonging to the pratyekabuddha vehicle, and realisation belonging to the Great Vehicle. Realisation of beings' own karmic fruit is that, relying on pure or impure karma committed as its own cause, beings experience and receive the ripened fruit of that karma across the ocean of birth and death among the five destinies. Realisation belonging to the śrāvaka vehicle relies first on taking refuge, then on the very adornments of a renunciant, and unfolds into five realisations: of the ground, of wisdom, of purity, of the fruit, and of merit.

items.title: Section: Three Grounds, Nine Wisdoms, and the Fastest Path to Liberation

items.zh: 地證得者，謂有三地。一、見地，二、修地，三、究竟地。智證得者，謂九智。一、法智，二、種類智，三、苦智，四、集智，五、滅智，六、道智，七、此後所得世俗智，八、盡智，九、無生智。淨證得者，謂四證淨。果證得者，謂四沙門果。功德證得者，謂無量、解脫、勝處、遍處、無諍、願智、無礙解、神通等。如是一切，應知如前已廣分別。又聲聞乘證得因者，謂得世間離欲之道，順解脫分、順決擇分所有善根。
items.en: Realisation of the ground names three grounds: the ground of seeing, the ground of cultivation, and the ultimate ground. Realisation of wisdom names nine wisdoms: wisdom of dharma, wisdom of its kind, wisdom of suffering, of origination, of cessation, of the path, conventional wisdom subsequently attained, wisdom of exhaustion, and wisdom of non-arising. Realisation of purity names the four kinds of pure faith. Realisation of the fruit names the four śramaṇa fruits. Realisation of merit names the immeasurables, liberations, mastery-bases, kasinas, the absorption free of contention, aspirational wisdom, unhindered understanding, and the higher knowledges. The cause of realisation belonging to the śrāvaka vehicle is the worldly path of freedom from desire, together with the wholesome roots of the branches conducive to liberation and the branches conducive to penetration.

blocks.text: Why the brahmins' liberation is not liberation, and the many senses of "truth", ending with a truth that cannot be spoken at all.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the brahmins take the Brahmā heavens of the first meditation as final liberation, but though these are free of desire they are not free of the three realms. Buddhist realisation is final, without falling back, stainless, and at ease.
Master Cháng Bǎi: holding a mistaken view to be liberation is "nominal seeking"; taking what is not skilful wisdom for skill, one pursues the absorptions as if they were release.
It encompasses all of defilement and purity, cannot be refuted, is easy to enter, and keeps practice from going wrong.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one must penetrate the intention, the Buddha's unspoken meaning. (Untranslated, 0653c18: "true meaning is the gateway of principle": undistorted, as it really is.)

Established truth is the four noble truths; truth realised within, where speech ends, is "non-established". Master Cháng Bǎi: the ultimate is free of marks, but once spoken it has marks. (Untranslated, 0653c28: worldly convention sets up houses, pots, armies, numbers, self, and beings; convention of principle sets up aggregates, elements, sense-fields; convention of realisation sets up the fruits.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary beings receiving karmic results is "realisation of karmic fruit". The wisdom attained afterwards is conventional and uses language.
"Once spoken, the ultimate has marks." Every teaching is a finger pointing; the treatise never forgets it.

quiz.q: What problem does Master Cháng Bǎi point out with taking the Brahma world as ultimate?
options: the Brahma world does not exist and is only imagined, so that nobody can be born there at all
the Brahma world still has sensual desire like this one
the Brahma world's lifespan is too short for practice
though free of desire, it is not free of affliction and still falls back to the desire realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the brahmins take the Brahma heavens of the first absorption as final liberation, but though these are free of desire they are not free of affliction, and one falls back to the desire realm.

quiz.q: What four features mark the renunciants' realisation?
options: culminating in the Brahma world, no falling back, free of desire, and cool
culminating in nirvana, never falling back, entirely free of stain, and entirely at peace
meaning not empty, shown to others, wording clear, enjoying wisdom
faultless, right hearing, right reflection, right cultivation
quiz.why: The treatise lists nirvana as culmination, no falling back, freedom from stain, and ease. Each point answers one fault of the brahmins' realisation: Brahma world, falling back, defilement, and suffering.

quiz.q: What are the further five in the distinction of seeking?
options: nominal, ultimate, observational, without skilful means, and with skilful means
natural, vowed, deluded, averse, and discerning seeking, which are at once seeking after existence and the distinction here
seeking alone, present, future, discerning, and heading towards attainment
seeking desire, existence, pure conduct, the nominal, and the ultimate
quiz.why: The treatise's further list is nominal, ultimate, observational, seeking without means, and seeking with means. The natural seeking and the rest belong to seeking after existence. The five of seeking desire are missing from the English and not tested.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi, following the commentary, explain nominal seeking?
options: a mistaken view takes it for liberation; though free of desire, it is not final liberation
one first sets up a name and then practices truly according to it
seeking worldly reputation with no thought of liberation
reciting names alone without calm or insight
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: to give rise to a mistaken view that this is liberation is called nominal seeking. Such a practitioner may be free of desire, yet it is not final liberation, and this is said of other paths.

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give for seeking without skilful means?
options: not knowing how to use skilful words for others and practising only for oneself
practising alone with no teacher to guide one
pursuing the four absorptions and four formless states as liberation, never reaching true nirvana
being too poor to make offerings to the Three Jewels
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: taking what is not skilful wisdom for skill, one walks a mistaken path of liberation, pursuing the four absorptions and four formless states as liberation, and so never realises true nirvana.

quiz.q: By which four purities is inner knowledge supreme?
options: purity of body, speech, mind, and heart, for inner knowledge purifies all of them
purity of meaning, wording, teacher, and disciples
purity of precepts, concentration, wisdom, and liberation
embracing all defilement and purity, unrefuted, easy to enter, and practice unspoiled once entered
quiz.why: The treatise lists encompassing all meanings of defilement and purity, being unrefuted by others, being easy to enter, and practice remaining unspoiled once entered. All four concern the doctrine's meaning.

quiz.q: Through which gateway is the gateway of true meaning discerned?
options: the gateway of intention, since true meaning lies in what the Buddha implies
the gateway of the inconceivable
the gateway of avoiding two extremes
the gateway of realisation
quiz.why: The treatise pairs true meaning with avoiding two extremes, realisation with the inconceivable, and teaching with intention. The first three gateways are each settled by one of the latter three.

quiz.q: Which purity does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate with the four truths?
options: ease of entry: the four truths are so simple that anyone grasps them on hearing with no practice
unspoiled practice: those who practice them never regress
embracing defilement and purity: covering both, and able to turn defilement into purity
being unrefuted: others dare not debate the truths
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: taking the four truths as an example, they embrace all principles of defilement and purity, worldly and transcendent, and can turn defilement into purity. This illustrates the first purity.

quiz.q: Why, says Master Cháng Bǎi, is the gateway of teaching settled by intention?
options: because all teaching is mere expedient and none of it is true
because teaching must fit the listeners' ages
because teaching needs prior assent from the community
one must grasp the Buddha's unspoken meaning to grasp the teaching
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one must penetrate the intention, the Buddha's unspoken meaning; if one penetrates the intention of the words, one can penetrate the gateway of the Dharma's teaching.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say established truth is?
options: the suchness of all phenomena, since it is the truth of all things and so is called established truth
truth established by worldly agreement
the four noble truths, suffering as suffering, and so on through the path as path
the object of wisdom purified of the cognitive obstruction
quiz.why: The treatise answers that established truth is the four noble truths. Suchness is the answer to the next question, non-established truth, and the two must not be exchanged.

quiz.q: Besides the three worldly conventions, what is the fourth kind?
options: non-established truth, since suchness itself is a fourth kind set up by names
the convention of ultimate truth, namely the ultimate truth itself
the convention of reasoning
the convention of worldly agreement
quiz.why: The treatise adds the convention of ultimate truth, namely the ultimate truth itself, to the three worldly conventions. The definitions of those three are missing from the English and so are not tested.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish established and non-established truth?
options: what language sets up is established; what is realised within, beyond words, is non-established
what the Buddha spoke is established and what masters say is non-established
worldly reason is established; other paths' reason is not
what three vehicles share is established; what is Great Vehicle only is not
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the true meaning set up by language and words is called established truth, and the truth realised within, where the way of speech is cut off and mental activity ceases, is called non-established truth.

quiz.q: Why is the ultimate called a convention, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the ultimate is free of marks, but expressed in words it has marks, so it is a convention
because the ultimate simply is the conventional with no distinction at all
because everyone in the world agrees upon it
because the ultimate can be realised only in this world
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ultimate truth should be a state free of marks, but when expressed in words it has marks, and for that reason it is called the convention of the ultimate.

quiz.q: What are the four realisations the treatise lists?
options: the grounds of seeing, cultivation, the ultimate, and merit, the śrāvaka's stages which extend also to the other vehicles
ground, wisdom, purity, and fruit
beings' karmic fruit, the śrāvaka vehicle, the pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Great Vehicle
aspiration, compassion, perfections, means of gathering
quiz.why: The treatise lists the realisation of beings' karmic fruit and of the three vehicles. Ground, wisdom, purity, fruit, and merit are the five within the śrāvaka vehicle, and aspiration and the rest belong to the Great Vehicle.

quiz.q: What is the seventh of the nine wisdoms in the śrāvaka vehicle's list?
options: wisdom of exhaustion, for the order puts non-arising first and exhaustion seventh
the conventional wisdom attained afterwards
wisdom of its kind
wisdom of the path
quiz.why: The treatise's list runs dharma, kind, suffering, origination, cessation, path, the wisdom attained afterwards, exhaustion, and non-arising. The seventh therefore stands between the wisdom of the path and the wisdom of exhaustion.
